Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexTel Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants are reminded that management may make forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexTel Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the Q3, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth.

Our achievements include robust results in our Content and Media segment, where revenues hit $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, outpacing guidance thanks to subscriber gains, ARPU increases, and solid ad performance. Streaming and SVOD brought in $1.6 billion, a 25% jump from the ad-supported tier launch now at 35% of paid users, generating $450 million from those at $5.99 a month. Linear affiliate fees were steady at $850 million with renewed deals featuring 3-5% escalators, while advertising added $350 million, up 12%, powered by data from our 150 million wireless subs. Profitability shone with $750 million in EBITDA at a 27% margin, up 300 basis points, and $550 million adjusted operating income at 20%, aided by 15% lower content costs per hour from rights resets like NBA adjustments and $100 million in AI recommendation synergies boosting retention 18%. We hit 52.3 million global paid streaming subscribers, adding 2.8 million nets—the best since our Peacock pivot—with blended ARPU at $12.49 up 8% YoY, churn at 1.8% down 40 basis points, and ad-tier subs at 18.2 million. North America led with 38 million subs and $2.1 billion revenue from sports like our NFL alternative averaging 4.2 million viewers; EMEA grew to 8.5 million with $450 million from UEFA rights and Vodafone bundles; APAC/LATAM added 5.8 million for $250 million via Globo and Indonesian 5G. We're pushing live premiumization with $500 million in sports/news rights, edge computing for 10ms latency gaming, and 40% wireless bundles at $18+ ARPU. Q3 guidance: $2.85-2.95 billion revenue, 26-28% margins, 2.5-3 million adds.

We are also seeing substantial growth from network investments, deploying $2.8 billion in capex, 28% of revenue up 12% YoY, with $1.82 billion or 65% to 5G buildout. Full-year target $10.5-11 billion total, $6.5 billion 5G-focused. We've reached sub-50ms latency over 85% U.S. footprint covering 280 million people, 45,000 5G sites including 12,000 urban small cells, 98% NSA coverage, 42% SA rollout. Open RAN at 15% new sites cuts capex 20%, 30% RAN virtualized, TeleMedia Edge for 10ms AR/VR with Disney boosting engagement 25%. U.S. C-band full in top metros drove 4.2 million 5G adds; Europe added 3,500 sites despite hurdles; APAC FWA ARPU 15% above broadband. Returns show 8% higher ARPU, 22% bundle growth for $450 million incremental, AI maintenance saving 10% opex. Capex peaks 2025 at $11.5 billion then tapers.

Further, we are concentrating on spectrum assets, holding 168 MHz average low/mid-band U.S., 40 MHz 600 MHz, 80 MHz C-band, 2.5 GHz leases, 1.2 GHz mmWave, plus Canadian JV. Utilization at 78% TTM up 26% YoY, mid-band 85% at 4.2 b/Hz, low-band 65%, mmWave 92%. Consumer 55%, enterprise/FWA 28%, media 17%. Northeast 91%, Southeast 87%, rural 52%. Data up 28%, 5G 65% base. DSS/carrier agg at 70% sites +25% capacity, refarmed 20 MHz PCS, AI SpectraOptix +18%, Open RAN 25%. Plans: 2025 lease 30 MHz C-band, FWA 3 million subs; 2026-27 FCC Auction 110 $1.5 billion; 6G $500 million, satellite integration. Targets 82% YE24, 88% YE25 for ARPU $58.

Additionally, service revenue grew to $28.4 billion, +5.2% YoY or 5.7% organic. Wireless $17.2 billion +4.1%, ARPU $52.47 +2.9%, 678k postpaid adds, 112k prepaid. 5G SA 85%, C-band 250M POPS, FWA 1.2M. Broadband $6.8B +7.8%, ARPU $68.20 +3.6%, 412k residential adds, FTTP 32M passed. Enterprise $4.4B +11.6%, ARPU $112.40 +6.8%, $1.2B contracts like Walmart $450M, JPM $300M.

We are also improving our cost of revenue management, at $4.8 billion up 7% YoY but flat QoQ, 42% of revenue down 200 bps. Network ops $2.496B +9%, content $1.344B +12%, CPE/field $720M -2%. Savings from AI energy -11%, windowing -6%. NA $3.6B, Europe $720M, APAC/LATAM $480M. Q4 guide $4.9-5.0B.

We are strategically investing in free cash flow, generating $8.4 billion FY23 up 18%, ops cash $16.7B, EBITDA $22.1B. Capex $8.3B down 7%. Utilization: $4.6B shareholder returns ($3.2B buybacks, $1.4B dividends +10%), $2.1B debt to 2.3x, $1.3B growth M&A/media, $400M cash to $5.2B. FY24 guide $9-9.5B.

Finally, EBITDA margins hit 38.2% up 140 bps, Q4 guide 39.5-40.5%, FY25 40-41.5%. Efficiencies $250M YTD, mix shift, FWA/media. Headwinds content/inflation offset by renewables, bundles.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $28.4 billion, representing a 5.2% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $10.8 billion, resulting in a margin of 38%. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $2.8 billion, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure. Free cash flow remains strong, building on last year's $8.4 billion generation, with ongoing deleveraging and returns. Cost trends are favorable, with efficiencies driving margin expansion toward our Q4 39.5-40.5% guide and FY25 40-41.5%. Service revenues across wireless, broadband, and enterprise all advanced, as Sarah noted, supporting our outlook.

Lisa Patel: Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage and increasing network capacity, achieving sub-50ms latency across 85% of our U.S. footprint and 45,000 sites live. We're also investing in advanced technologies like network slicing, edge computing, Open RAN at 15%, and vRAN at 30% to support new applications and services including AR/VR media delivery. Our network uptime and reliability remain high at 99.99%. We are also improving spectrum utilization to 78%, with dynamic sharing, refarming, and AI management pushing efficiency higher, targeting 82% by year-end.

David Kim: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth and improved customer satisfaction scores this quarter, with postpaid adds over 678,000 and churn at 0.82%. Our bundled service offerings are resonating well with customers, including 5G with streaming at 40% attach, and we're focused on providing a seamless and personalized customer experience. We are also focused on increasing enterprise penetration, with 11.6% revenue growth and key wins like Walmart for edge computing.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to enhance our network and services. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations and improve efficiency, including SpectraOptix for spectrum and predictive maintenance. We are also working on developing new products and services that leverage 5G and edge computing, like TeleMedia Edge for low-latency content. Our R&D efforts are concentrated on 6G sensing, private networks, and media personalization with GenAI tagging.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding private 5G networks and SD-WAN growth?

David Kim: Thanks, John. Enterprise is a high-margin priority, with Q3 revenues at $4.4 billion, up 11.6% YoY, accelerating from Q2. Large enterprise grew 14%, mid-market 9%, with wireless ARPU at $112.40, up 6.8%, on 245,000 mobility adds and $1.2 billion in contracts—including $450 million 5G SA with Walmart for edge and robotics, $300 million SDx with JPMorgan, and Siemens IoT for 2.5 million devices. Our 5G ANS with uMIMO and aggregation holds 15% private network share, EPoPs in 50 metros with AWS. TeleWave ONE AI orchestration lifted margins 250 bps to 52%. APAC +18%, LatAm +8%. Pipeline $15 billion, targeting 11-13% FY25 growth via CBRS and licensed slices for media production. We're outpacing via telco-media edge over pure plays.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding capex and cost of revenue trends?

Michael Chen: Thanks, Emily. Inflation and rates are headwinds, but manageable given our profile. COGS at $4.8 billion rose 7% YoY to 42% of revenue, but efficiencies like AI energy savings 11% to $210 million and content windowing -6% offset ramps in 5G opex $1.1 billion and sports licensing $720 million +18%. Capex $2.8 billion disciplined at 28% revenue, shifting to opex via vRAN for 18% IRR. Union caps at 3.5%, renewables 20% sites cut power 5%. Refinanced debt at 4.2%, leverage 2.3x. FY25 margins 40-41.5% embed mitigations, with $1.2 billion FCF add from 16-17% capex intensity.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing energy efficiency in network operations?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Mike. Sustainability is core, with AI orchestration cutting energy 11% or $25 million YoY, renewables at 20% sites, targeting 20% total gains by FY25. Predictive maintenance and SDN/NFV align with AT&T pledges. Metrics: opex reductions, site efficiency b/Hz, Scope 1/2 emissions down via edge/5G multicast 40% video savings. Success via 300 bps gross margin expansion FY25, tying to FCF $9-9.5 billion.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in NexTel Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
